To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The air bubble structure of natural rimed ice is characterized by y-shaped closed pores.

we have developed a new technique to investigate the air bubble structure of ice particles and that we have found that the air bubble structure in natural ice particles is different from that of artificially rimed ice particles.

(i) 3-D imaging and quantitative analysis of the pore structure of ice particles is now possible with a spatial resolution of a few microns, and (ii) the pore structure of natural ice particles differs from that of ice particles artificially produced in the wind tunnel.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new methods and techniques to measure and characterize the micro-structure of snow and ice particles.
the 3-D structure and morphology of ice particles.
the 3-D imaging and the quantitative analysis of the air pore structure inside ice particles.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the air bubble structure in ice particles can be studied by means of synchrotron micro-CT, and that the cryo-stage developed at the SLS is a powerful tool to study the morphology of ice particles at high spatial and temporal resolution.
the air bubble structure of natural graupel is not well understood.
the pore structure of graupel is a function of the riming process and the thermal history.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
3-D data on individual pore structures in natural and artificial ice samples are now available.
the cryo-stage setup allows for the first time to study the pore structure in natural ice particles at the micron scale and with a high resolution.
we are able to provide 3-D data of ice samples at a resolution of 3 μm and a voxel size of 2.5 μm3.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the pore structure of ice particles is not only a function of the riming process, but also of the temperature history during sampling and measurement.
synchrotron micro-tomography provides a unique opportunity to study the 3-D pore structure of ice particles at micron resolution and to quantify the porosity of ice particles.
synchrotron radiation-based X-ray microtomography is a powerful tool for the 3-D imaging and quantitative analysis of the internal air bubble structure of ice particles.
